addendum:
## 📖 Added definitions (glossary backfill)

| Term | Definition |
|------|-----------|
| SWE | SWE refers to software engineering, specifically the tasks and agents involved in developing and modifying software. |
| R2E | None |
| ORACLE | ORACLE refers to a theoretical upper bound for patch selection, achieved when ground-truth tests are used to pick the best candidate patch. |
| GT | GT refers to ground-truth tests, which are the hidden, canonical tests used to determine if a patch is truly resolved. |
| PR | PR refers to a problem statement or pull request description, which serves as the initial input for an agent to understand a task. |
| MECE | MECE refers to criteria that are Mutually Exclusive and Collectively Exhaustive, meaning each rubric item covers a distinct aspect and together they cover all relevant aspects of correctness. |
| PROMPT | PROMPT refers to instructions or queries given to a large language model, guiding its output or behavior. |
| RANDOM | RANDOM refers to a lower bound for patch selection, achieved when a candidate patch is chosen uniformly at random from all available candidates. |
| YAML | A structured data format used by the agent to output its repository-grounded checklist, which must be parseable by a safe-loading function to be considered a valid scoring attempt. |
| SFT | A training process used to distill rubric-generation and patch-classification capabilities into smaller open-source models using expert-generated trajectories. |
| CWM | An open-source model used as a generator for agentic rubrics and candidate patches during the evaluation experiments. |
| IMO | An expression indicating a subjective assessment of the paper's strongest finding regarding the high utility of rubric judgments when they disagree with ground-truth tests. |
| RM | A reward model used to provide feedback for reinforcement learning, which the paper suggests rubrics could serve as a denser and more auditable alternative to. |
| FC | One of the four rubric axes, specifically the File Change category, which evaluates a patch's correctness based on the scope and locality of its edits. |
| HF | A research platform and repository used to check for datasets, models, and citations associated with the paper's public availability. |
| JS | A technology that gates the paper's project landing page, preventing automated tools from fetching the site's content. |
